STEP 2 - Ruler: The white bowl has a diameter of roughly 15 cm (cereal-bowl size, comparable to the width of the wooden board it sits on, which is about 4-5 cm wide). Using the bowl as a 15 cm vessel: area = 3.14 x (7.5)^2 ≈ 177 cm^2. Note that the almonds are about 2.5 cm long and 1.5 cm wide, which is consistent with this scale.

STEP 3 - Items: Whole roasted almonds (about 20-22 pieces, some split or halved).

STEP 4 - Area: The almonds cover roughly 40% of the bowl's surface area, a little under half of the visible white area. Almonds: 40%.

STEP 5 - Volume: 40% of 177 cm^2 ≈ 71 cm^2. Almonds pile about 1.2 cm high on average. Gross volume ≈ 71 x 1.2 ≈ 85 ml.

STEP 6 - Grams: Almonds are whole nuts with substantial air gaps. Bulk density for dense nuts is about 0.6 g/ml. 85 ml x 0.6 ≈ 51 g. Cross-check: 20 almonds at about 1.2 g each is about 24 g, so the count-based estimate is lower. The count-based figure is more reliable for individual pieces, so I'll use about 30 g, which is roughly 22 almonds at 1.2-1.4 g each.

STEP 7 - Energy: Raw/roasted almonds are about 579-600 kcal per 100 g. Using 580 kcal/100 g: 30 g x 5.8 ≈ 174 kcal.

STEP 8 - Sanity check: About 20-22 almonds is a plausible small snack portion, roughly 30 g and about 170-180 kcal, which matches a typical single serving of almonds. Nothing else is on the plate, so the total is the almonds alone.

Total: about 30 g, about 175 kcal.
